reading.title: Why Vague Predictions Feel Personal
reading.intro_zh: 这篇拓展阅读延续 Lesson 60“模糊预言为何像被说中”的主题，介绍真实的心理学现象——巴纳姆效应（Barnum effect），改编自权威参考资料 EBSCO Research Starters。
passage: Why do horoscopes, fortune-tellers, and online personality quizzes so often seem to describe us with uncanny accuracy? Psychologists trace much of this illusion to the Barnum effect, a tendency to accept broad, flattering generalizations as if they had been written for us personally. In a famous demonstration, the psychologist Bertram Forer gave his students what they believed was an individually tailored personality profile. In reality, every student received the same text, much of it lifted from a horoscope booklet. Asked to rate how well the description fitted them from zero to five, the students returned an average of 4.3, only to discover that their portraits were identical.

The phenomenon takes its name from the nineteenth-century showman P. T. Barnum, who built a fortune on the art of pleasing gullible audiences. The label itself was coined later, when the psychologist Paul Meehl coined the term "Barnum statements" in 1956. Such statements work because they are elastic: a line like "You enjoy being with friends, but sometimes you value your quiet time" fits almost everyone, yet each reader supplies private memories that make it feel intimate and specific.

Several cognitive habits reinforce the deception. People are inclined to embrace positive information about themselves, and they tend to trust pronouncements that appear to come from an authoritative source. Consequently, once a prediction is dressed up with the apparatus of expertise, our critical guard tends to drop. Recognizing the Barnum effect does not mean dismissing every personality test as worthless; rather, it invites a healthier skepticism. Before we marvel that a forecast came true, it is worth asking whether the same words could just as easily have fitted a thousand strangers.

questions.question: What is the main point of the passage?
options: Vague, general statements feel personally accurate because of a psychological tendency called the Barnum effect.
Horoscopes are usually written by trained professional psychologists.
P. T. Barnum invented the first scientific personality test.
Online quizzes are more reliable than printed horoscopes.
questions.explanation_zh: 全文围绕巴纳姆效应展开：人们会把模糊、笼统的描述当成专门为自己写的，从而觉得很准。这是主旨。

questions.question: In Forer's demonstration, what did all of the students actually receive?
options: A different profile written individually for each person.
A blank sheet with no description at all.
The same identical text, much of it taken from a horoscope booklet.
A written diagnosis from a professional fortune-teller.
questions.explanation_zh: 短文明确说 every student received exactly the same text, much of it lifted from a horoscope booklet，即所有人拿到的是同一份、且大量取自星座小册子的文字。

questions.question: According to the passage, why do Barnum statements feel intimate and specific to each reader?
options: Because the statements secretly contain the reader's real name.
Because each reader fills the elastic wording with private memories of their own.
Because the statements are checked against official records.
Because only one type of person ever reads them.
questions.explanation_zh: 短文解释这类陈述富有弹性（elastic），适用于几乎所有人，而 each reader supplies private memories that make it feel intimate and specific，即读者用自己的私人记忆去填充，才觉得贴切。

questions.question: What can be inferred about why a prediction wrapped in 'expertise' is more convincing?
options: Such predictions are always proven correct by later events.
People lower their critical guard when something seems to come from an authoritative source.
Experts are legally required to tell the truth about the future.
Algorithms cannot make mistakes about people.
questions.explanation_zh: 短文说人们倾向相信看似来自权威来源的说法，所以一旦预言被披上专业外衣（水晶球、算法、术语），our critical guard tends to drop，由此可推断权威外表让人放松警惕。

questions.question: In the passage, the word 'elastic' (in 'they are elastic') most nearly means
options: made of rubber and able to stretch physically.
extremely difficult to understand.
officially approved by scientists.
flexible enough to be stretched to fit many different situations.
questions.explanation_zh: 这里 elastic 是比喻用法：紧接着说这类陈述 applies to almost everyone，说明它有弹性、可以套到很多不同的人/情况上，即“灵活、可伸缩适用”。

writing.intro_zh: 今天把 Lesson 60 的五个高价值句式提升到 B2+：用 decided to 写经过权衡后的主动选择，用 After I had..., ... 写先完成一件事再发生第二件事，用 will be arriving 写已安排好的未来到达，用 The moment..., ... 写一发生就紧接着发生，用 in less than... 写紧迫的时间。每句都要更复杂、更抽象。

patterns.title: decided to ...
patterns.source: I decided to visit a fortune-teller called Madam Bellinsky.
patterns.focus_zh: decided to 用来写“(经过考虑后)决定去做某事”，比 just went 更能表现主动、深思熟虑的选择。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：在描述一个你原本将信将疑的现象（如星座、算命 app 或性格测试）时，写你最终决定亲自验证它是否真的准确。
patterns.sample: Curious yet sceptical, I finally decided to test whether the personality quiz could really describe a stranger as accurately as it described me.
patterns.tip_zh: decided to 后面接动词原形；可以用 test, investigate, examine, challenge 等更书面的动作动词。

patterns.title: After I had ..., ...
patterns.source: After I had given her some money, she looked into a crystal ball.
patterns.focus_zh: After I had... 用过去完成时清楚标出第一件事先完成，随后第二件过去动作才发生。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写你先完成了某个准备步骤（如比对、记录或核实信息）之后，才发现那个看似神秘的预言其实有平凡的解释。
patterns.sample: After I had compared the so-called prophecy with my friend's, I realised that the two predictions were almost word for word identical.
patterns.tip_zh: After I had 后面用过去分词，如 compared, examined, recorded；逗号后面接随之发生的第二个过去动作。

patterns.title: will be arriving ...
patterns.source: She will be arriving this evening.
patterns.focus_zh: will be arriving 用将来进行时，适合写一个已经安排好、注定要发生的到达。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写一位远道而来的亲戚或一支代表团将在某个具体且重要的时刻抵达，并点出这次到来的意义。
patterns.sample: My grandmother, whom none of us has seen for almost a decade, will be arriving on the morning train just before the family reunion begins.
patterns.tip_zh: will be arriving 后面常接较具体的时间、地点或从句，让安排好的未来显得更确定、更有分量。

patterns.title: The moment ..., ...
patterns.source: The moment you leave this tent, you will get a big surprise.
patterns.focus_zh: The moment 表示“一……就……”，强调两个动作几乎同时、紧紧相连地发生。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写当你刚意识到某个“预言”的真相，一个平凡的解释立刻浮现，让神秘感瞬间消失。
patterns.sample: The moment I noticed how vague the wording truly was, the whole prediction stopped feeling magical and seemed almost embarrassingly ordinary.
patterns.tip_zh: The moment 引导第一个动作；逗号后面写几乎同时发生的第二个动作，可加入抽象的心理变化。

patterns.title: in less than ...
patterns.source: Your sister will be here in less than an hour.
patterns.focus_zh: in less than... 写出时间非常紧迫，表示“不到……以后(就)”。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写一个重要时刻（如展示、截止、列车或会面）很快就要到来，并说明这种紧迫感带来的压力或后果。
patterns.sample: The judges announced that every team would have to present its final findings in less than fifteen minutes, and panic spread across the room.
patterns.tip_zh: less than 后面接时间长度，如 fifteen minutes, half an hour, two days；可再补一个分句写出后果。
